name.back_horizon: From behind, looking at the horizon

alt.profile_view: Illustration: a person standing in profile at a railing, looking out at the landscape. The camera is at their side, at chest height.
alt.back_horizon: Illustration: a person seen from behind, looking toward the horizon over the sea. The camera is behind them, slightly to one side.
alt.low_angle: Illustration: a person standing in front of a monument and looking up at it. The camera is close to the ground, tilted upward.

tips.viewpoint: Morning or late-afternoon light is usually softer than at midday. Stand in profile near the edge and turn your face toward the view, while the photographer shoots from your side at chest height so the panorama fills the background.
tips.waterfront: A low sun around sunrise or sunset gives warm light and long reflections on the water. Turn your back to the camera and look toward the horizon, keeping the horizon level and away from the middle of the frame.
tips.monument: Coming early usually means fewer people in front of the building. The photographer crouches close to the ground and tilts the camera up so the monument rises above you; look up toward the top rather than at the lens.
tips.default: Soft morning or late-afternoon light is usually the most flattering. Stand slightly in profile, look into the scene rather than at the camera, and leave some space in front of your gaze.
